request.spec:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each sheet now has its own "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there, and `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V2__sheet_today.sql`, adds a `today` date to each sheet. A new sheet gets the real date when it is first loaded.
- **Server:** loading a sheet now returns its today along with its id. A new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{id}/today`, changes it and rejects a missing or malformed date with a 400. `SheetService.today(id)` gives the sheet's today for any later date logic or default date.
- **Front end:** `home.ts` shows the date (`sheet-today`) with a date input (`sheet-today-input`) and a save button (`sheet-today-save`). If the date is refused, the reason appears in the existing `sheet-error` element, and it clears as soon as the form is edited or saved again.

Right now the app holds only sign-in and sheets, so nothing else depends on the date yet. Nothing else uses the real clock: `LocalDate.now()` is called only when a new sheet is created, and as a fallback in `SheetService.today(id)` if the sheet doesn't exist. The spec doesn't ask for an audit record when the date changes, so I didn't write one.
